issues.title: U.S. Loses Measles-Free Status After 26 Years, a Major Public Health Setback
issues.summary: A certified medical assistant administering the MMR vaccine to patients at the Parkside Pediatrics practice in Spartanburg, SC, on January 30, 2026. The United States has lost its measles elimination status after 26 years, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) announced on November 17. U.S. measles cases reached 5,412 in 2026, the highest total in 35 years, according to Centers for Disease C
issues.content_html:
• The United States has lost its measles elimination status after 26 years, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) announced on November 17.
  • U.S. measles cases reached 5,412 in 2026, the highest total in 35 years, according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) data.
  • About 96% of this year’s measles cases were in people who were unvaccinated or had unknown vaccination status.
  • Two doses of the MMR vaccine are about 97% effective and offer the best protection against measles, according to the CDC.

The United States has officially lost its measles elimination status, a major public health achievement that was secured 26 years ago.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s (WHO) regional office for the Americas, determined that measles has spread continuously in the U.S. for more than 12 months. On November 17, PAHO announced the end of the country’s measles elimination status, which it has held since 2000.

“Losing a measles elimination status has broader implications than losing a public health designation,” PAHO’s director, Jarbas Barbosa, MD, MPH, PhD, said in a media briefing. “It means the virus has circulated for a prolonged period of time, putting families and communities at risk of a preventable illness, hospitalization, and death.”

PAHO’s review examined measles spread starting January 20, 2025, when the first person became ill in a large West Texas outbreak, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

CDC data show 5,412 confirmed measles cases this year as of November 12. That’s the highest annual total since 1991 and more than double the 2025 count of 2,289 cases.

Andi Shane, MD, chief of pediatric infectious diseases at Children’s Healthcare of Atlanta, called the U.S. losing measles elimination status “a public health alarm that we are not being effective and we’re not controlling measles as well.”

The measles virus is highly contagious. It spreads through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. People can catch it in a room up to two hours after an infected person has left, according to the CDC.

What losing measles-free status means for the U.S.

“There’s really been very little measles in the United States over the past 25 years until January 2025,” William Moss, MD, a professor of epidemiology at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, told Healthline.

Losing the status itself doesn’t change much about daily life for most Americans, Moss said. The concern is the measles outbreaks, hospitalizations and deaths behind the loss, he said.

He called the loss “a big red flag” after “enormous efforts over the past 26 years” to keep the status.

A country loses its elimination status when there is “uninterrupted circulation of the same virus genotype and lineage for 12 months or more,” according to PAHO. Shane explained it this way: “For the past 12 months in the United States, we’ve had ongoing circulation of the measles virus and person-to-person transmission is occurring.”

Canada lost its elimination status in November 2025, and the U.K. and five European countries lost theirs earlier in 2026.

The U.S. can regain the status. “Other countries have done that,” Moss said. Brazil, which lost its status in 2019, regained it in November 2024. Venezuela, which lost its status in 2018, regained it in 2023, according to PAHO.

How the U.S. eliminated measles: A timeline

Before the measles vaccine, measles infected an estimated 3 million to 4 million Americans each year, according to the CDC. Among reported cases, about 400 to 500 people died each year, 48,000 needed hospital care, and 1,000 developed encephalitis, or brain swelling.

Here’s a timeline of measles elimination in the U.S.:

  • 1954: Scientists isolate the measles virus during an outbreak in Boston (CDC).
  • 1963: The U.S. licenses its first measles vaccine (CDC).
  • 1968: An improved, more weakened live-virus vaccine goes into use. (CDC).
  • 1971: The U.S. licenses the combined measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine (CDC).
  • 1978: The CDC sets a goal to eliminate measles by 1982. The country misses the deadline, though reported cases drop 80% between 1980 and 1981 (CDC).
  • 1989: After outbreaks among vaccinated school-age children, national health groups recommend a second MMR dose for all children (CDC).
  • 1994: The Vaccines for Children program, created by Congress in 1993, begins providing free vaccines to eligible children (CDC).
  • 2000: The U.S. declares measles eliminated (CDC).
  • Jan. 20, 2025: The West Texas outbreak begins (CDC).
  • Nov. 2026: PAHO rules the U.S. has lost its elimination status.

Moss said elimination efforts “really intensified” after a large outbreak from 1989 to 1992. Part of that push was “really promoting school entry vaccination checks,” he said.

“That was one of the key policy changes that I think allowed for measles elimination in the United States.”

Every state and Washington, D.C., require children to be vaccinated against measles to attend school, though exemptions vary by state, according to the nonprofit health policy organization KFF.

Why measles made a comeback

Fewer kindergartners are getting the MMR vaccine, according to the CDC.

Kindergarten MMR coverage fell from 95.2% in the 2019–2020 school year to 92.4% in 2025–2026. About 280,000 kindergartners started the 2025–2026 school year without records showing they had completed the MMR series, the CDC reported.

Shane said “95 out of 100 people need to be protected against measles” for a community to get herd protection.

“So since we’ve been below that for many, many months, that is also contributing to the loss of our elimination status,” she said.

“It takes two things to have a measles outbreak,” Moss said. A community needs low vaccine coverage, and someone with measles has to enter it and “start the chain of transmission,” he said.

About 96% of this year’s cases were among people who were unvaccinated or had unknown vaccination status, up from 93% in 2025, according to the CDC.

Moss said many of those cases are adults.

“This is particularly true in Pennsylvania, where about two-thirds of the cases are in adults,” he said. Many never got vaccinated as kids and grew up while measles was rare, so they never built natural immunity, he said.

He noted that having so many unvaccinated adults puts pregnant people and adults with chronic conditions like lung disease at risk of serious illness. The U.S. has already seen “dozens of pregnant women actually getting infected during pregnancy,” he said.

Infected parents can also spread measles to young children and grandparents, Shane said. Shane traced much of the hesitancy to the pandemic. “With COVID there’s been an overall distrust in vaccines and vaccination that initially started with COVID but has now spread to other vaccines,” she said.

Moss pointed to the federal government. “We know what it takes to achieve and sustain elimination. We have the expertise. We have the resources,” he said.

He cited staff cuts at the CDC and said messaging from Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and President Donald Trump has undermined vaccine confidence. He called federal messaging on vaccines “really mixed and weak.”

Moss also criticized the President’s August 10 executive order calling for the MMR vaccine to be split into separate shots for each disease.

“There’s no justification for that, and those vaccines don’t even exist in the United States,” he said.

Measles vaccine offers best protection against the disease

Measles may cause ear infections, diarrhea, pneumonia, encephalitis and, in some cases, death, according to the CDC. The disease may also weaken the immune system for weeks to a year after recovery, raising the risk of flu, COVID-19, or RSV, Shane said. “It’s not a benign childhood disease,” Moss said.

The best protection against measles is two doses of the MMR vaccine, which are about 97% effective, according to the CDC. Shane said, “There are not very many other things we do in life that give you such great protection.” People who missed doses can still catch up, she added. “If you just don’t know or can’t tell, there’s no harm — as long as you’re eligible — in getting another MMR vaccine.”

Shane added that “parents really want to do the right thing for their children.”

“We know that the MMR vaccine — that’s the vaccine that provides protection against measles — is a safe vaccine. It’s a very effective vaccine,” Shane said.

Babies under 12 months are too young for the vaccine. “So they depend on the protection of the people around them,” Shane said.

The CDC recommends a first MMR dose at 12 to 15 months and a second at 4 to 6 years. Babies 6 to 11 months old who will travel internationally should get an early dose, and adults without proof of immunity should get at least one dose, according to the CDC.

To stop the outbreaks, Moss said the U.S. will need to “increase vaccine coverage, particularly in those communities that have had long-standing low vaccine rates.”

So far, the response has been “more reactive than proactive,” Moss said. Public health teams scramble once an outbreak starts, he said, and he wants more outreach to at-risk communities before measles arrives.

“I am worried about the ability of the United States to regain measles elimination status in the current climate,” Moss said.

issues.title: New Guidelines Recommend Routine Prostate Cancer Screening for Men Over 50
issues.summary: New ACS guidelines encourage men over 50 to get regular PSA tests to screen for prostate cancer. miodrag ignjatovic · E+/Getty The American Cancer Society (ACS) now recommends prostate-specific antigen (PSA) screening every 2 years starting at age 50 for men at average risk, and annually starting at age 45 for those at higher risk, including Black men and men with a family history of prostate canc
issues.content_html:
• The American Cancer Society (ACS) now recommends prostate-specific antigen (PSA) screening every 2 years starting at age 50 for men at average risk, and annually starting at age 45 for those at higher risk, including Black men and men with a family history of prostate cancer.
  • The updated guidance reflects new evidence that regular PSA screening can reduce the risk of dying from prostate cancer by 13% and help detect potentially aggressive cancers before they spread.
  • If PSA levels are elevated, additional testing, including prostate MRIs and biomarker tests, can help determine whether a biopsy is necessary, potentially reducing unnecessary procedures.

As rates of advanced prostate cancer continue to rise, the American Cancer Society (ACS) has issued new guidelines recommending routine prostate cancer screening for many men starting at age 50.

The updated recommendations, published November 12 in CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians, mark a shift from the organization’s previous emphasis on shared decision making about whether to undergo screening.

Under the new guidelines, the ACS recommends regular prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing beginning at age 50 for men at average risk of prostate cancer and age 45 for those at higher risk.

Advances in MRI technology and biomarker testing may also help doctors determine which men need further testing, potentially reducing unnecessary biopsies and overtreatment.

How Often Should Men Get Screened for Prostate Cancer?

The ACS last updated its prostate cancer screening guidelines in 2010, when conflicting research findings raised questions about whether the benefits of PSA screening outweighed the potential harms.

At the time, the organization emphasized informed, shared decision making between patients and healthcare professionals.

However, longer-term follow-up studies have since provided stronger evidence of the benefits of early detection, prompting the ACS to conduct a systematic review and update its recommendations.

The authors of the report noted, “In making these recommendations, we recognize that PSA testing is only the first step in a screening cascade that includes secondary testing of men with an elevated PSA level and treatment decisions for men diagnosed with prostate cancer.”

The new guidelines recommend a PSA test every 2 years for men ages 50–69 with an average risk of prostate cancer.

The recommendation for those at high risk is a PSA test every year starting at age 45.

For men ages 70–74, the ACS recommends individualized decision making. If an individual chooses to be screened, the ACS recommends a PSA test every 2 years until the age of 74.

Ramkishen Narayanan, MD, Director of the Center for Urologic Health at The Roy and Patricia Disney Family Cancer Center at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline that screening shouldn’t automatically be ruled out for men over 75.

“[A] point worth noting is that for men over 75, their PSA history as well as their individual clinical scenarios should be evaluated, and that PSA should not be discouraged in this group of men if their life expectancy and clinical history warrant a PSA check.”

Who is at a higher risk for prostate cancer?

According to the ACS, approximately 1 in 8 men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer during their lifetime.

Individual risk depends on age, race/ethnicity, and other factors:

  • Prostate cancer is more likely to develop in older men, with an average diagnosis age of 68.
  • Black men are also at a higher risk than those of other races.
  • Men with a family history of prostate cancer, particularly a father or brother who has been diagnosed, may be at higher risk.

Why the ACS Updated Its Prostate Cancer Screening Guidelines

Prostate cancer diagnoses in the United States increased by around 3% per year between 2014 and 2022, according to the ACS.

The rise in diagnoses, particularly advanced-stage prostate cancer, has renewed attention on the importance of regular screening.

“[The] current state of prostate cancer screening guidelines is vague and generalized. This has led to ambiguity, disagreement, and variation of opinion among healthcare providers and institutions in their approach to men’s health,” said S. Adam Ramin, MD, board certified urologist, urologic oncologist, and medical director of Urology Cancer Specialists in Los Angeles, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report.

The updated ACS guidelines drew partly on findings from a 2025 follow-up of the European Randomized Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer (ERSPC), which found that regular PSA screening was associated with a 13% reduction in prostate cancer deaths over 23 years.

A 12-year ERSPC follow-up in 2012 also suggested that regular screening was associated with a decrease in metastatic prostate cancer diagnosis, which is another finding that influenced the updated guidance.

“Prostate cancer can take many years, even decades, to become clinically significant, so it takes a long time for us to see the consequences of changes in screening practices,” Taylor Goodstein, MD, assistant professor of urology in the College of Medicine at the University of Cincinnati, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline.

“With longer follow-up from randomized trials, we now have more convincing evidence that PSA screening reduces the risk of dying from prostate cancer,” she said.

“The ACS guidelines are important now because they drive home the most important point that prostate cancer screening saves lives,” said Narayanan.

What PSA Levels May Require Further Testing?

Healthcare professionals use PSA levels to help determine whether additional testing for prostate cancer may be necessary.

The ACS recommends further testing for men under 70 with PSA levels of 3 ng/mL or higher.

For those ages 70 and older, the ACS recommends further testing if their PSA is 6.5 ng/mL or higher. This is because PSA levels tend to be naturally higher in older men.

You can speak with your healthcare professional to find out more about PSA cutoff levels.

How New Screening Guidelines Could Improve Prostate Cancer Outcomes

Goodstein told Healthline that the ways this new guidance can change the outlook for prostate cancer are simple.

“If we screen men, we can catch troublesome cancers early, before they have a chance to spread,” she said.

Goodstein also emphasized how much the evaluation process has changed. In the past, an elevated PSA level often led directly to a biopsy.

Today, doctors generally repeat the PSA test within two weeks to three months to confirm the result. If PSA levels remain elevated, additional testing, including a prostate MRI or validated biomarker test, can help determine whether a biopsy is necessary.

Narayanan told Healthline, “The new guidelines will hopefully remove any confusion about the value of PSA screening and encourage prostate cancer screening as an integral part of a man’s ‘checkup’.”

He added that it is worth noting that the DRE (digital rectal exam) adds little value to the initial prostate cancer screening and is no longer something that men should fear.

“Adoption of this set of specific guidelines standardizes the approach to screening for prostate cancer. It provides a unified effort among all levels of healthcare. It most likely will increase the chances of finding prostate cancer in earlier stages and lead to improved cancer treatment outcomes,” said Ramin.

issues.title: Mind Games: My ‘Secret’ to Enjoying Coffee Without Anxiety
issues.summary: Adding L-theanine to your morning coffee could help relieve caffeine-induced side effects like anxiety and jitters. Oleg Breslavtsev/Moment/Getty Images This article is part of a mental health content series called “Mind Games,” in which Healthline editor Morgan Mandriota draws on personal experience and research to challenge misconceptions, reduce stigma, review trends, and share hot takes and le
issues.content_html:
This article is part of a mental health content series called “Mind Games,” in which Healthline editor Morgan Mandriota draws on personal experience and research to challenge misconceptions, reduce stigma, review trends, and share hot takes and lessons learned about what it means to be mentally well.

Coffee and I don’t exactly have the best relationship.

My morning cup tends to give me jitters, worsen my anxiety, and keep me up until 2 a.m. if I drink it past noon. As an already anxious human, the last thing I need is to exacerbate my symptoms, even if it’s coming from a delicious source.

Over a year ago, I noticed that my anxiety was higher than usual. I was also tossing and turning and waking up at all hours of the night for weeks on end.

One night in particular, I woke up every hour for 8 hours. Naturally, I wanted to blame it on the full moon or anything other than my beloved coffee, but alas, I realized that my caffeine consumption was the most likely culprit.

Could I have aimed to set a strict drinking schedule to see if that fixed things? Sure. But instead, I decided to quit cold turkey and undergo an experiment to see how I’d feel going coffee-free for the first time in years.

Over the next 8 months, I’d swap my coffee station for a matcha setup, dabble in exotic herbal blends from my local teahouse, and become a self-proclaimed tea connoisseur. Lo and behold, my anxiety eased up, and my sleep quality improved, too.

Fast forward to 4 months ago, when I hopped back on the coffee train. But this time, I’m relying on a handy amino acid to help avoid anxiety and other unwanted side effects: L-theanine.

Health and wellness touch everyone’s life differently. This is one person’s story. The views and opinions expressed are those of the speaker and do not necessarily reflect the views or positions of Healthline Media and should not serve as a substitute for medical advice from a healthcare professional.

How L-theanine can help offset coffee side effects

L-theanine is mainly found in green and black tea and one type of wild mushroom. The mental health benefits of L-theanine consumption are an emerging area of research, but one 2024 review found that consuming around 200 to 400 milligrams (mg) may help relieve symptoms in people with anxiety disorders.

Still, anecdotal reports suggest there may be benefits of adding L-theanine to coffee. Over the last 5 years, the combo has been gaining traction on Reddit and TikTok for managing caffeine-related side effects.

Despite an overwhelming amount of rave reviews online, I couldn’t find much research to support these claims, so I spoke with a neurologist to see if they had any thoughts.

“This trend has real science behind it,” said Fawad Mian, MD, who is board certified in neurology, clinical neurophysiology, and sleep medicine and the founder of Ascend Regenerative.

“Controlled studies show caffeine plus L-theanine improves focus and attention more than caffeine alone, and some suggest it softens caffeine’s side effects, like tiredness, headaches, and blood pressure spikes,” Mian said. “It smooths caffeine’s effects but doesn’t erase them, so it’s not a license to drink more coffee,” he added.

With all of this in mind, especially after realizing just how calm I was while drinking black and green teas during my coffee break, I decided to give it a try.

So, does it help? Here’s my personal experience

After about 4 months of “testing,” I’ve found that adding L-theanine to my coffee works extremely well for me.

No more anxiety, scatterbrain, shakiness, or staying up until 3 a.m. And no lifestyle overhaul needed. The supplement, which I prefer in liquid form, has become a seamless addition to my daily routine.

Every morning, I make a fresh batch of French press coffee with (strong) local beans, then I squeeze some L-theanine into my cup.

I’ve noticed that I get the usual coffee benefits like improved focus and concentration, plus a nice, calm, stable energy throughout the day.

Even if I drink it until 2 p.m., I’m fighting to keep my eyes open at night before I finally fall asleep around 10. Perhaps this is because L-theanine may also support quality sleep.

The L-theanine product I use and love

Mindful L-Theanine Drops is the liquid supplement that I use every day.

I add a one-second squeeze (which contains 200 mg of L-theanine) into my morning coffee, then I’m good to go. I even started carrying a bottle in my bag just in case I get a latte from a coffee shop on a whim.

You can also add it to a glass of water, a cup of tea, or another drink of your choosing. It’s unflavored, so it doesn’t alter the taste of your drinks. Real secret stuff.

Out of curiosity, and because I’m a natural skeptic and overthinker, I asked Mian if my positive experience could be a placebo effect, or if I’m seeing real results.

“Expectation may play a small role, but the effect is biologically plausible,” he said. “L-theanine boosts calming brain activity that offsets caffeine’s stimulation, and 200 mg matches the doses used in studies.” However, he noted that it doesn’t speed caffeine clearance, so drinking coffee only in the morning still matters for sleep quality.

While L-theanine is generally safe to consume, it’s best to speak with a healthcare professional first, especially if you’re pregnant, nursing, receiving cancer treatment, or taking blood pressure medication or sedatives.

“Choose a third-party tested brand, and if caffeine makes you anxious, cutting back is still the simplest fix,” Mian added.

So, if you’re anything like me and drinking coffee also leads to anxiety and jitters for you, I highly recommend trying this supplement once you get the green light from your doctor. It’s been working for me. It may work well for you, too.

💌 Over to you: I’d love to hear your thoughts on this. Does coffee also give you unwanted side effects? Have you tried L-theanine to remedy them? Let me know, or ask any questions about my experience by emailing me here.

issues.title: How to Plan Your Holiday Meals in a Year of Unprecedented Recalls
issues.summary: While many people are concerned about foodborne illness and food recalls, experts say with the right preparation, foods are safe to eat. LumiNola · E+/Getty About 60% of U.S. adults say they’re more concerned about foodborne illness this year than in previous years. However, experts say past recalls don’t mean entire food categories need to be avoided. Experts recommend checking FDA and USDA recal
issues.content_html:
• About 60% of U.S. adults say they’re more concerned about foodborne illness this year than in previous years. However, experts say past recalls don’t mean entire food categories need to be avoided.
  • Experts recommend checking FDA and USDA recall lists before shopping or preparing holiday meals to ensure ingredients aren’t affected by active recalls.
  • Safe holiday food preparation involves four basic practices: clean, separate, cook, and chill to reduce the risk of foodborne illness.
  • Holiday leftovers should be refrigerated within 2 hours and can typically be stored safely for 3 to 4 days.

Following a series of high-profile food recalls and outbreaks this year, many Americans may be concerned about keeping their families safe from foodborne illness during the holidays.

In fact, according to a recent national survey by Orlando Health, around 60% of U.S. adults say they’re more concerned about foodborne illness this year than in previous years.

Although several major foodborne illness outbreaks have ended and their associated recalls are no longer active, food safety remains an important concern. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimates that 48 million people in the United States experience foodborne illness each year.

However, there are simple steps you can take to reduce the risk of foodborne illness when preparing holiday meals and storing leftovers.

Are foods safe to eat after a recall has ended?

While there were several food recalls in the United States over the summer, two of the largest involved Salmonella linked to jalapeños and Cyclospora linked to lettuce.

These outbreaks prompted widespread recalls and raised concerns about the safety of certain foods, particularly fresh produce.

Although health officials have since declared the major outbreaks over, some consumers may still be hesitant to purchase foods associated with previous recalls.

Even with this declaration, you may still feel nervous about purchasing certain foods, but experts say you don’t need to worry.

“Here in the United States, we have the safest food supply in the world. The recent recalls show that our food safety system is working,” said William Schaffner, MD, Professor, Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University.

Michelle Routhenstein, preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished, told Healthline that past recalls do not mean entire food categories need to be avoided. The important thing is whether the specific product you have matches a current recall, based on details such as brand, lot number, package size, and expiration date.

“You should enjoy familiar foods, including properly cooked poultry, washed fruits and vegetables, and pasteurized dairy products,” she said. “The key is checking relevant recalls and practicing safe food handling.”

Check for recalls

“Before shopping or cooking, review FDA and USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture) recall information and compare any relevant notices with the labels on your ingredients,” said Routhenstein.

Check the pantry and freezer, too: something purchased months ago may still be affected.

“Stay alert to any news reports about food recalls and use good food preparation practices. Those simple actions should keep your holidays happy and safe,” said Schaffner.

Consumers can sign up for food recall alerts through the FDA or visit FoodSafety.gov for recall information from both the FDA and USDA.

How to safely prepare and store holiday foods

Schaffner emphasized the importance of following safe food-handling practices when preparing everyday meals and holiday gatherings.

“Remember the longstanding advice: keep food hot or cold. Avoid long times at room temperature,” he said.

Routhenstein advised focusing on four basics: clean, separate, cook, and chill.

  • Clean: Wash hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds and rinse produce under running water. Avoid washing raw poultry, which can spread bacteria through splashing.
  • Separate: Keep raw meat and poultry away from ready-to-eat foods to prevent cross-contamination.
  • Cook: Use a food thermometer. Turkey and stuffing should reach 165°F (74ºC). Cooking stuffing separately is generally the safer option.
  • Chill: Refrigerate perishable foods within 2 hours of serving, or within 1 hour if the temperature exceeds 90°F (32°C).

How long can holiday leftovers sit out?

Schaffner noted the importance of refrigerating leftovers promptly rather than leaving them at room temperature for extended periods. He recommends clearing the table and refrigerating leftovers soon after the meal ends.

Routhenstein reiterated that you should refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours rather than leaving them out to cool.

Divide turkey into smaller portions and transfer sides and gravy into shallow containers to help them cool quickly, she advised.

Leftovers can typically be stored in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. If you don’t plan to eat them within that time, consider freezing them.

The important thing is to keep an eye out for any new recalls, practice food safety, and enjoy your holiday meals!

issues.title: Selling to friends
issues.summary: There are two versions, very different: FAVOR: This is what multi-level marketing preys on. You ask a family member or a friend to buy something, not because they need it, but because you do. This doesn’t always end well. Someone might want to further their relationship with you by doing you this favor, but if […]
issues.author: Seth Godin
issues.content_html:
There are two versions, very different:

FAVOR: This is what multi-level marketing preys on. You ask a family member or a friend to buy something, not because they need it, but because you do.

This doesn’t always end well. Someone might want to further their relationship with you by doing you this favor, but if the unspoken promise is that the item or service is worthwhile, the disappointment that ensues hurts everyone. Real estate brokers or middlemen in a bind often seek to build friendly relationships at the club or community meetings, but then try to leverage this friendship into a significant sale without doing the hard work of actually being the best choice.

TRUST: This is the sort of sale that happens when you begin with the benefit of the doubt but actually deliver a great outcome. You’ll know this is the case when the person who trusted you ends up testifying on your behalf to others.

“No pressure” is something that’s showing up more and more in the pitches I’m seeing. Of course, there’s no pressure! Just saying it implies that you wish there were.

If you’re asking for a favor, you’re not serving and you’re not selling. You’re trading.

And if you’re asking for trust, be prepared to honor the obligation it creates.

issues.title: Practical empathy
issues.summary: I don’t know what you know. I don’t want what you want, see what you see, believe what you believe. And that’s okay. In fact, it’s the only way to be of service, to make a sale or to cause a change to happen. Of course, we’re more intimate with our ideas, our products and […]
issues.author: Seth Godin
issues.content_html:
I don’t know what you know. I don’t want what you want, see what you see, believe what you believe.

And that’s okay.

In fact, it’s the only way to be of service, to make a sale or to cause a change to happen.

Of course, we’re more intimate with our ideas, our products and our approach than anyone else. We have a noise in our head, a narrative and a point of view we’ve spent our whole lives creating. It’s naive to believe that anyone else is completely in sync with us.

And so, our only opportunity is to go where they are, not to demand that they come to us.

Practical empathy isn’t primarily an act of kindness (though it’s an essential component of kindness.) Instead, it’s a direct and straightforward path from here to there. It’s how we create action, learning and change.

Marketing is the simple and brave act of going to where someone else might be, and helping them get to where they hope to go.

issues.title: Confusion about causation
issues.summary: It’s not difficult to develop an incorrect theory. Ice cream and spaghetti have more letters than tofu and celery, so therefore, foods with long names are more fattening than those with short ones. If you start moving forward with this theory, you’ll soon find outliers. Sugar only has five letters, and watercress has ten. If […]
issues.author: Seth Godin
issues.content_html:
It’s not difficult to develop an incorrect theory. Ice cream and spaghetti have more letters than tofu and celery, so therefore, foods with long names are more fattening than those with short ones.

If you start moving forward with this theory, you’ll soon find outliers. Sugar only has five letters, and watercress has ten. If we want to stick with our theory, we’ll have to come up with more and more complex reasons why we ignore some of the data and embrace the rest.

Of course, this is absurd.

And yet we do it all the time. Ornate explanations about the stock market, SEO or politics. Charts and graphs where we spend most of our time fitting a plot to a few dots, or amplifying the obscure to justify the theory.

A simple theory that matches the data is much more likely to accurately explain causation. It might not be a comfortable theory, or one that matches our trajectory, but it’s a better theory.

It turns out that the number of letters is completely irrelevant to how fattening a food is. I’m sorry you spent all this time on research, but you’re on the wrong path.

If you want to know why your marketing, your investments or your arguments are floundering, it might pay to reconsider the theory, not look for more data to justify the current one.

issues.title: How to track your brand's visibility in AI search [2026]
issues.summary: Marketers need to know how to track brand visibility in AI search because search has changed. AI-generated answers now show up earlier in the discovery journey, often before a traditional search result. In 2025, nearly a third of Gen Z consumers (31%) defaulted to chatbots or AI to find information online, according to HubSpot’s 2025 AI Trends for Marketers report , and it’s clear that AI search i
issues.author: Zoe Ashbridge
issues.content_html:
Marketers need to know how to track brand visibility in AI search because search has changed. AI-generated answers now show up earlier in the discovery journey, often before a traditional search result. In 2025, nearly a third of Gen Z consumers (31%) defaulted to chatbots or AI to find information online, according to HubSpot’s 2025 AI Trends for Marketers report, and it’s clear that AI search is growing — rapidly. In 2026, Google reported that AI Mode has over one billion monthly users, and queries have doubled every quarter since launch.

Failure to place brands in AI Overviews (AIO) or within AI search tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Claude is a failure to meet prospective buyers where they’re searching. That’s harmful to audience connection, conversion, and ultimately, revenue. Brands that show up in AI search are the ones that audiences consider. The ones that don’t simply disappear from the conversation, with no ranking position, no impression count, and no obvious way to tell.

This article breaks down what brand visibility is, how to track brand visibility in AI search, the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) that marketers need to pay attention to, and the best tools to support AI visibility tracking.

Table of Contents

  • What is AI search and brand visibility?
  • How to Track Brand Visibility in AI Search Right Now.
  • How to Track Brand Visibility in AI Search with the Right KPIs and Cadence
  • How to Track Brand Visibility in AI Search with a Repeatable System
  • How to Improve AI Search Visibility and Fix Inaccurate Answers
  • Best Tools to Track Brand Visibility In AI Search
  • How To Connect AI Visibility To Content And Pipeline
  • Frequently Asked Questions About Tracking AI Search Visibility
  • Tracking AI visibility isn’t optional anymore — search changed.

What is AI search and brand visibility?

AI search refers to search that takes place on AI platforms, like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, and Google’s AI Overviews. There are many more, and AI search platforms are growing. Unlike Google or other search engines, which return a list of links to click through, AI search engines answer questions directly. Those answers are lifted or paraphrased from trusted sources.

Brand visibility in AI search relates to the impressions that brands get within AI platforms. A brand mentioned or cited in AI in an answer has visibility. Brand visibility in AI search includes mentions, citations, sentiment, and accuracy. The goal is for brands to increase their visibility. They want to be cited and mentioned often, accurately, and favorably.

How to Track Brand Visibility in AI Search Right Now

The most basic way to check AI brand visibility is manually: Open ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Copilot. Ask the same set of questions across each one. Then, record whether the brand appears, how it’s described, and whether competitors show up instead. This is an easy starting point. But, it breaks down quickly.

A single spot check only captures one moment in time. That result reflects one user’s search history and personalization, not any broader trend. When multiplied across several platforms and hundreds to thousands of prompt variations, manual tracking becomes a task that nobody has time to maintain.

HubSpot ran an experiment testing hundreds of queries across AI chatbots, search engines, and social platforms. The experiment found that AI tools were noticeably weaker at handling specific, niche information, like details about a particular local business, than they were at answering broad or general questions. This is why prompts need to be tracked consistently — and ideally automatically. No one can infer how a platform or brand performs across the board just because it performs well in one prompt, particularly if that prompt is broad and general.

This is where dedicated tools come in.

Rather than replaying the same prompts by hand, tools built for AI brand tracking run them automatically, on a schedule, across multiple engines at once, then organize the results into a usable format, such as:

  • Which prompts triggered a mention.
  • Which sources got cited.
  • How sentiment trended over time.

Different tools approach brand visibility measurement in different ways; some focus narrowly on mention frequency, others build out fuller scoring models across multiple dimensions.

HubSpot’s free AI Search Grader is one example. The grader gives marketers a baseline read on AI visibility, and what it provides for free is pretty amazing. Here’s what the start of the report looks like.

While tools like AI Search Grader are excellent, there are limitations.

AI Search Grader captures a baseline read; it doesn’t track improvements or declines in trends. Ideally, most marketing teams will move from a one-time snapshot to ongoing tracking, so that they can adapt marketing strategy based on data.

Tools like HubSpot AEO provide ongoing tracking and data related to performance in AI search tools. It monitors brand mentions, citations, and sentiment across AI platforms continuously. With continuous tracking, marketing teams can see how efforts and campaigns have impacted visibility.

Here’s a look at a citations report, showing a brand’s domain performance versus competitors:

How to Track Brand Visibility in AI Search with the Right KPIs and Cadence

Switching between tools or KPIs will only provide inconsistent and confusing results. No two tools report the same numbers. All a tool can provide is a third-party overview of what’s happening with a brand’s visibility, and none of them are completely accurate.

Feedback from a tool should be treated as a directive, not absolute truth. What marketers are looking for are trends in the data, and that comes from consistent tracking using the same tool and the same metrics.

Now that caveat is out there, let’s look at KPIs:

Brand Mention Rate

Brand mention rate measures how often a brand appears in AI-generated answers. It’s a foundational metric; it’s calculated by dividing the number of AI answers that mention the brand by the total number of answers analyzed across a set of tracked prompts. A low mention rate indicates that AI platforms rarely surface the brand at all.

Here’s an example of a brand mention in ChatGPT. The mention of the brand is there, but there’s no clickable link:

Mentions and citations are not the same thing: an AI platform might mention a brand by name without linking to anything it owns, or it might cite a third-party review site instead of the brand’s own content.

Citation Rate

Citation rate measures how often AI answers link to or reference brand-owned sources. Tracking citation rates separately shows which domains and pages are actually earning a reference inside AI answers, which points directly to the content that needs to be built or strengthened.

Here’s an example of a brand citation in AIO. There’s an actual link, and if clicked, the user will visit the website of the cited source (in this case, HubSpot):

Source

Pro tip: To support citation rates, marketers can track actual clicks to the website from AI sources. I include this metric on all of my client reports. It reports to stakeholders that we’re getting cited, but also that these citations are turning into valuable actions for the business. Kyle Rushton-McGregor has a guide on how to track AI visits in GA4.

Sentiment and Accuracy

Sentiment measures how AI platforms describe a brand. It’s typically scored on a scale from negative to positive.

Accuracy is related to sentiment.

Marketers want their brands to appear accurately in AI.

A negative sentiment might not be a bad thing if it’s accurate. For example, if an AI platform describes a brand as ‘expensive compared to competitors’ and that brand has a premium price point, the sentiment reads as negative, but the description is accurate, and the brand probably wants to defer searchers looking for a cheap solution.

That said, marketers must manage brand sentiment and ensure that sentiment is overall positive. Brand sentiment can teach marketers about things customers are unhappy about. If marketing comes across a repeated negative sentiment, then they can share information with customer success or product development to try to change that narrative.

Share of Voice

Share of voice measures how often AI search platforms mention a brand compared to competitors across the same set of prompts. It’s important because if marketers look at their brand in isolation, the mention rate might look great, but comparing share of voice against competitors reveals the wider opportunities and potential.

A low share of voice relative to competitors shows where the gaps are and what brands need to do to close the gap.

How to Track Brand Visibility in AI Search with a Repeatable System

A repeatable system turns AI brand tracking from ad hoc checks into a data-driven marketing approach. With this approach, marketing teams can make strategic decisions based on data and trends, leading them to meaningful solutions that improve a brand’s visibility in AI search.

The following five steps give marketing and AEO (also called GEO) teams a framework to set up once and run on an ongoing basis.

1. Run a baseline visibility check.

Before setting up ongoing tracking, it helps to research and establish a starting point. Otherwise, marketing is creating a tracking system based mostly on feeling.

AI Search Grader helps measure brand visibility in AI search, scoring how ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity currently describe a brand across sentiment, presence quality, brand recognition, share of voice, and market position.

Marketers can use tools like AI Search Grader to get a big-picture overview of how their brand performs. They’ll start to build a picture of how the brand sentiment looks and where there might be opportunities.

And it’s free. So, marketing can run AI Search Grader for competitors to build a mental map of the wider AI search landscape. The beauty of AI Search Grader is that there are no limits, so marketing teams can use this free tool as much as they like. Every search in AI Search Grader builds research, curiosity, and insights that can be carried into the final plan.

2. Write consistent, structured prompts.

AI search tracking requires consistent prompts across multiple AI platforms. Like switching tools or KPIs, switching prompt wording between checks makes it impossible to tell whether a shift in results reflects a change in visibility or just a different question.

Marketing teams should write out the exact prompt list in advance, document it, and reuse the same wording every time a check runs. This is a lot easier when working with a tool, because the tools will categorize prompts and maintain the exact prompt over time, but if working manually, marketers need to manage it.

Tools like AI Search Grader can inspire prompt selection, but marketers don’t have to stop there. Existing keyword research is a great starting point, especially long-tail keywords in Google Search Console (GSC). Specifically, keywords that include problems and solutions for certain audiences, for example, “How do I solve [problem] in my [company]” or “how to fix [problem] in your forties.” Many keywords are already phrased as questions, or close enough that it’s not a leap to see how they’d translate into a query on an AI platform.

Talking directly to customers helps, too. Sales and customer success teams often have a good sense of the exact language prospects use when researching a purchase. If sales or customer support have a good relationship, they could even ask customers if they’d share their own AI chat history, which will surface real prompts marketing teams would not have thought to write themselves.

Important note: Asking for chat history could be invasive. This ask can only work if there’s a customer relationship that’s already been built.

Once marketing has the prompts locked down, it’s time to decide where to track them and how to manage them.

3. Map the core AI platforms and build a prompt taxonomy.

Core AI platforms include ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, and Google AI Overviews. However, most brands don’t need to track every single platform, which is good news for brands working with tighter budgets. Some tools charge a base fee for ChatGPT tracking, with add-on costs for each additional AI platform.

How to Decide Which Platforms to Track

For one of my clients, who had a limited budget, we focused solely on ChatGPT. We used a marketing report to decide which platforms to pay the most attention to. I tracked clicks from all the core platforms, as well as a few others. Clicks from ChatGPT far exceeded all other core AI platforms, with over 87.18% of total AI visits coming from ChatGPT. Claude and Gemini were next with 4.49% each, then Copilot at 2.56% and Perplexity at 1.28%.

Important note: Some AEO tools don’t charge to track data from additional AI tools, so check what the tools allow users to track as part of a free or paid package, and what costs extra.

HubSpot’s AEO tracks brand visibility across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity as part of the same $50-a-month package, with no extra charge to add the second or third platform once a prompt allowance is purchased. Other tools, like Profound.ai, charge $99/month to track ChatGPT, then $399/month to track three platforms.

For my client, HubSpot AEO is ideal because it’s affordable and tracks the major AI platform they need — ChatGPT.

Once marketing has the platforms to track, marketers need a prompt taxonomy (a way of organizing prompts). The prompt taxonomy should include brand, competitor, category, task-based, and comparison prompts.

Check out the example below.

4. Set a tracking cadence and automate ongoing monitoring.

With prompts written, categorized, and platforms selected, the last piece is deciding how often to check them.

Cadence matters as much as the metrics themselves. Weekly reviews support baseline AI brand monitoring, giving marketing and SEO teams a steady read on trends without demanding daily attention. Daily checks make sense during active optimization sprints — testing content changes, responding to a citation gap, or catching a sentiment issue that needs a fast fix.

Tools like HubSpot AEO automate this cadence, running the same prompt set across engines on a schedule and organizing the results so nobody has to manually replay the same questions week after week.

5. Route visibility data into CRM and content workflows.

If marketing can route visibility data into CRM and content workflows, AI visibility can turn from a vanity metric into a revenue input. With this, AI reporting becomes highly engaging to stakeholders, who ultimately care about revenue because it shows how AI search performance and pipeline are integrated.

This ‌routing is where most standalone AEO tools fall short entirely. The fact that HubSpot AEO is built on a CRM gives it an incredible advantage.

With an integrated CRM and AI tool, visibility data becomes a system where it gets routed to the people and workflows that can respond to it.

Here’s how:

  • HubSpot Smart CRM stores AI visibility properties, prompt clusters, and dashboard data, keeping visibility metrics in the same system as the rest of a brand’s customer and campaign data instead of siloed in a separate tool.
  • HubSpot Content Hub turns visibility gaps into content briefs and refreshes, so a low mention rate on a topic becomes an assignment rather than a stat that nobody acts on.
  • HubSpot Marketing Hub connects AI visibility efforts to campaign reporting and attribution, closing the loop between AI search visibility and the pipeline and revenue outcomes leadership actually cares about.

How to Improve AI Search Visibility and Fix Inaccurate Answers

Once marketing tracks prompts and performance, it will reveal gaps, and once gaps are identified, marketing can construct a data-driven plan to close them.

The next section details some best practices to address common visibility and accuracy issues.

Strengthen entity consistency across the web.

AI platforms build their understanding of a brand from many sources at once, such as:

  • The company website.
  • Review sites.
  • Social profiles.
  • Directories.
  • Press mentions.

AI platforms pull information from across the web to create one synthesized answer. The best thing marketing can do is control the controllable, and, where possible, ensure that information is consistent and accurate.

For example, be consistent with the brand’s name, description, location, and core offering. Naturally, marketing can’t control everything, like a bad or incorrect review, but marketing combats negative sentiments with the truth. Plus, marketing can work with product teams or customer success to identify issues and prompt resolution.

Ultimately, AI platforms have a hard time confirming what’s correct if multiple versions of a narrative exist. That increases the odds of an inaccurate or inconsistent mention.

Build content that earns citations.

Page structure has been a topic in the world of search for many years. We all know that structuring pages well, with titles, headings, and body text, is good, but it’s possible to take things a step further for AI search.

For example, marketing can get super-specific about audiences and problems, creating pages around the exact problems buyers are having.

Answering questions directly, providing solutions, and backing them with claims with concrete details and data all make a page easier for AI platforms to lift from and cite.

For more information about writing for AI engines, read: How to Write Content that Generative AI Search Engines Will Cite, According to Experts

Correct inaccurate AI answers.

Inaccurate AI answers should trigger content updates, correction requests, and follow-up monitoring, especially if the inaccuracy is on owned media, like the brand’s website or Google Business Profile.

Tip: If you’re not sure where a piece of information has come from, because AI hasn’t cited anything, try searching for the information in Google and see what ranks. Look at your own website for inaccuracies. Let’s say an AI platform has cited your brand’s package as costing $69, but this price is over two years old, search in Google “site:yourwebsite.com $69.” This search would look for mentions of “$69” on your website. It’s possible the price is listed somewhere, like an old blog.

Expand presence across multiple channels.

AI platforms draw on a wide mix of sources, so a brand’s visibility is rarely built from its website alone. Active participation in industry discussions, consistent responses to reviews and feedback, and a presence across the platforms where a brand’s category gets discussed all contribute to how AI models perceive and describe a brand. The broader and more consistent that footprint, the more material AI platforms have to draw an accurate, favorable picture from.

Monitor for recurring issues.

A single inaccurate answer might be a one-off. The same issue appearing across multiple prompts or platforms is a pattern worth escalating. When negative sentiment or a factual error keeps showing up, it is worth routing that finding beyond marketing — into product, customer success, or support — since the underlying cause is often something those teams are better positioned to fix.

Best Tools to Track Brand Visibility In AI Search

The four tools below cover the full range of what a marketing team needs, from foundational SEO work to dedicated AEO tracking.

Marketing Hub SEO Marketing Software

This article focuses a lot on AEO and AI visibility, but AEO is not separate from SEO. Regardless of how many people search in AI, traditional SEO is still critical, more popular than AI search tools, and impactful on the sources that are mentioned and cited in AI tools.

Therefore, SEO tools are still a must.

Marketing Hub’s SEO tools lay the groundwork on which AI visibility depends‌.

Source

HubSpot’s SEO tools include an audit that surfaces prioritized fixes for on-site issues like broken links, missing meta descriptions, and thin content, then groups related content into topic clusters designed to build topical authority around core subjects rather than isolated keywords. It also pulls keyword data directly from Google Search Console, so marketing teams can see which queries are already driving organic traffic and which ones represent gaps worth closing.

What I like: Having data in one place is efficient. HubSpot allows integrations with Google Search Console, so data can be managed and checked from one place. The SEO recommendations are easy to use, written in plain English, and even have impact scores (high, medium, and low). The system names the person responsible for the fix, meaning tasks that keep SEO flowing are easily delegated.

HubSpot AEO

Source

HubSpot AEO is undoubtedly the core tool for ongoing AI visibility tracking. It provides marketers with four key capabilities:

  • A brand visibility score that tracks how often a brand appears across a set of tracked prompts.
  • Prompt-level tracking that shows the exact response each engine gave for each question.
  • Citation analysis that breaks down which domains and content types are earning references.
  • Competitor share of voice that shows how a brand’s mention rate stacks up against named competitors on the same prompts.

HubSpot AEO suggests a starting prompt set based on a brand’s industry, competitors, and business context, which can then be edited or expanded by the marketing humans in the team. Everything is trackable across major AI platforms like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity, and results roll up into a dashboard that tracks visibility over time rather than showing a single static score.

Finally, recommendations turn the data into specific next actions:

  • Create a new page or update an existing one
  • Publish a LinkedIn post
  • Reach out to a third-party site for a mention.

One limitation worth flagging: Claude and Copilot are not currently tracked. For brands where either platform sends a meaningful share of AI referral traffic, that’s a real coverage gap to weigh before committing.

What I like: The recommendations and AI visibility tracking within HubSpot are absolutely useful and critical to marketing, but the real differentiator, in my opinion, is the CRM. Most AEO tools operate as a standalone dashboard, disconnected from what actually happens after a brand shows up in an AI answer.

HubSpot AEO doesn’t have that problem because it’s built on top of HubSpot CRM. The connection between marketing performance and sales matters more than ever. A visibility score sitting in isolation is just a vanity metric. What pays bills is knowing whether a mention, a citation, or a jump in share of voice actually turned into a contact, a deal, or revenue.

HubSpot AI Search Grader (free)

AI Search Grader is the place to start if marketing is new to AI brand visibility or tracking AI in any form.

AI Search Grader runs a one-time scored assessment of how ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity currently characterize a brand, scoring five dimensions out of a 100-point total:

  • Sentiment (40 points): The overall tone AI models use when describing a brand, evaluated across three layers: general tone, how that tone shifts across different topics and use cases, and the credibility of the sources shaping that characterization.
  • Presence Quality (20 points): How substantively AI platforms discuss the brand (“mention depth”), the quality of the sources feeding that understanding, and the overall richness of data available about the brand.
  • Brand Recognition (20 points): How widely the brand is recognized within AI training data itself.
  • Share of Voice (10 points): How often the brand is mentioned relative to competitors within the same set of responses.
  • Market Position (10 points): How the brand is positioned competitively compared to others in its category, based on how AI platforms describe its standing in the market.

The scoring is weighted toward sentiment because how a brand is described tends to matter more to buyers (and therefore marketing and sales) than simply whether it’s mentioned at all.

AI Search Grader runs against pre-set queries automatically, without requiring the marketer to write any prompts. ChatGPT and Gemini responses draw on model training data, while Perplexity’s results come from live web search, since Perplexity works differently under the hood. The tool also benchmarks a brand’s score against competitors, so the output reads more like a competitive snapshot than an isolated report card.

The trade-off is exactly what its name suggests: it’s a grader, not a tracker.

AI Search Grader captures one moment and doesn’t retain history or show trend lines, so running it repeatedly over time won’t build the kind of longitudinal data a brand needs to prove whether a strategy is working.

What I like: I always start with AI Search Grader for a benchmark, and I use it in pitches to show a brand exactly where it stands before any investment is made. It’s also my go-to when I want a read on competitors, but I can’t justify paying to track brand mentions in AI, like a secondary competitor that I’m curious about but don’t need tracked with full accuracy over time.

HubSpot AI Search Sensor

Source

HubSpot AI Search Sensor takes a different angle from the other three tools on this list.

It doesn’t track a specific brand at all.

It’s a free public dashboard built from anonymized HubSpot customer data, tracking industry-wide shifts in AI search behavior through three views:

  • AI-Referred Traffic Trends shows aggregate weekly traffic from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity, useful for checking whether a brand’s own traffic dip reflects something brand-specific or a broader industry pattern.
  • AI Visibility Benchmarks by Industry shows visibility and citation share for a handful of representative brands across ten industries, giving a sense of what a “good” score looks like in a given category.
  • Citation Share Trends breaks down which content types (blog posts, product pages, listicles, and more) and which source channels (owned, earned, review sites, affiliate, and more) are earning citations, and how that mix is shifting week over week.

There’s also a daily Answer Engine Volatility Tracker, scoring how much answer engine behavior is shifting on a given day, from Calm through Extreme.

What I like: Marketing teams can use this broad data alongside their own AEO data: if a brand’s visibility score drops on a day when the volatility tracker also spikes, that points to a model update or algorithm shift rather than a brand-specific problem.

How to Connect AI Visibility to Content And Pipeline

AI visibility data should shape the content calendar directly. A low mention rate on a category prompt signals a content gap worth filling. A low citation rate on an existing page suggests the page needs restructuring, not replacing. A competitor winning share of voice on a comparison prompt means there’s a comparison page worth building.

This shifts content strategy from “what ranks” to “what gets cited and recommended.” The two overlap but aren’t identical — a page can rank well in Google and still get ignored by an AI platform if it doesn’t answer the question directly enough to lift and cite.

Connecting that data to pipeline is what makes the work defensible.

When visibility metrics sit in HubSpot’s CRM and marketing tools rather than a standalone dashboard, a content brief generated from a visibility gap can be tracked through to the campaign it supported and the deals that followed. That’s the difference between reporting a visibility score and reporting what the score was worth.

Frequently Asked Questions About Tracking AI Search Visibility

Which AI platforms should I prioritize first?

The AI platforms that any brand should prioritize should be decided based on data. Pull AI referral traffic from internal analytics. It will show which platform is dominating over the others and sending the most traffic. That platform is the one worth prioritizing first. However, from experience, the platforms to prioritize will probably be ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, or Copilot, plus AI Overviews within Google Search.

What’s the best way to organize prompts for consistent tracking?

Prompts hold up best when organized into a taxonomy covering brand, competitor, category, task-based, and comparison types, with the exact wording documented and reused every time a check runs.

How do I correct outdated or wrong information about my company in AI answers?

If an AI platform is describing a brand based on outdated pricing, an old feature list, or an incorrect description, the fix usually starts with the brand’s own website or Google Business Profile, since that’s the material marketing teams have the most control over.

How can I attribute AI search visibility to revenue?

Attribution starts with routing visibility data into the same system as customer and campaign data, rather than leaving it in a standalone dashboard. When AI visibility properties, prompt clusters, and citation data sit inside a CRM, marketing teams can connect a visibility gap to the content brief it produced, and that content to the campaign, contact, or deal that followed.

How often should we review and refresh our prompt library?

The prompt library itself needs a slower refresh cycle, revisited quarterly or whenever a brand launches a new product, enters a new category, or notices its keyword research and customer language shifting. Prompts that no longer reflect how buyers actually ask questions stop producing useful data, even if the tracking cadence around them stays consistent.

Tracking AI visibility isn’t optional anymore — search changed.

Failing to track AI visibility in 2026 and beyond is a failure to keep up with search, serve clients, and keep your brand at the top of prospective buyers’ minds.

For anyone starting from zero, HubSpot’s free AI Search Grader remains the fastest way to get a baseline read on where a brand currently stands, and HubSpot AEO is the natural next step once that baseline is set and marketing are ready to track mentions, citations, and sentiment across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity, all while feeding directly into the same CRM already running a brand’s marketing and sales data.

In my own client work, I’ve been tracking AI visibility for a year or two, and things are trending up for every single client, even those in niche B2B. For me, the major benefit of starting now is that brands have a benchmark and can see clearly how the search landscape is changing and how it’s impacting brand and visibility.

issues.title: Claude AI for marketing: How teams use it with HubSpot

issues.author: HubSpot Staff
issues.content_html:
I’ve been experimenting with Claude AI for marketing workflows over the past year, and it’s now my go-to assistant. In this field, AI use is close to universal: 98% of marketing teams use it in some way, according to HubSpot’s State of AI in Marketing report. For campaign marketers, that might look like turning a product announcement into a week of social posts, tightening ad copy to fit character limits, or pressure-testing campaign messaging before a stakeholder review.

But Claude only knows what you tell it. It can’t automatically see which contacts converted, which campaigns generated pipeline, or what customers keep asking your support team, so even sharp output can miss what’s actually happening in your business.

The HubSpot connector for Claude brings your HubSpot CRM data into the conversation and lets Claude act on it, like drafting a marketing email or creating a follow-up task directly in your account. This guide covers how to set up the connector, the marketing workflows and prompts it supports, how to govern its use, and when a dashboard is the better choice.

Table of Contents

  • What is Claude AI for marketing?
  • Why Connect Claude to HubSpot?
  • How to Connect Claude to HubSpot Using the HubSpot Connector for Claude
  • Claude AI for Marketing Workflows Inside HubSpot
  • Claude Prompts for Marketers Using HubSpot Context
  • How to Govern Claude AI for Marketing and Measure Impact
  • When to Use Dashboards Instead of Claude AI for Marketing
  • Frequently Asked Questions About Claude AI for Marketing

What is Claude AI for marketing?

Claude AI for marketing means using Claude, Anthropic’s AI assistant, to handle the writing, research, and analysis work that campaigns depend on. Claude helps marketers draft, analyze, and summarize work, such as writing and editing first drafts, turning meeting notes into briefs, and assembling campaign readouts from numbers in separate analytics tools. It can also pull current information from the web, which makes it handy for early-stage market research.

As with all large language models (LLMs), the quality of Claude’s output depends heavily on the context it receives. Anthropic’s prompting guidance compares Claude to a sharp new employee with no background on how your team operates, and it recommends telling Claude who the output is for and how it will be used.

Claude works well on its own for one-off drafting and research. It becomes far more powerful once it can read your real customer records, campaign results, and engagement history.

Why connect Claude to HubSpot?

Picture a marketer asking Claude why last quarter’s webinar series underperformed. Without a link to HubSpot, Claude can only work with what gets pasted into the chat: an exported spreadsheet, a few copied metrics, a paragraph describing the audience. Each fresh analysis means exporting and explaining that background again, and the answer stops wherever the export does.

Connected workflows move that context gathering out of the marketer’s hands. The HubSpot connector for Claude links HubSpot context to Claude, giving it read access to contacts, deals, campaigns, marketing emails, and other records, scoped to each person’s current HubSpot access rights. Logged calls, meetings, emails, tasks, and notes are readable too, unless the account has Sensitive Data turned on. The webinar question can now pull event records, follow-up activity, and campaign attribution data into a single answer.

The connection also runs in reverse. Claude can create and update HubSpot records, such as changing a deal stage or adding a task, from the chat window, though it can’t delete data.

HubSpot Smart CRM unifies customer context and campaign records. It sits beneath Marketing Hub, Sales Hub, and HubSpot’s other core products as their shared database, showing where each contact stands at every point in the relationship. Claude then works from one consistent record rather than fragments stitched together from separate tools. Connected AI workflows improve personalization and execution for that reason.

Getting there takes a one-time setup in Claude’s connector settings.

How to Connect Claude to HubSpot Using the HubSpot Connector for Claude

The HubSpot connector for Claude is free, but it requires a paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise) and an active HubSpot user account on any plan, including free. Super Admins and users with App Marketplace Access permissions can connect immediately; everyone else needs Super Admin approval first.

Then, in Claude:

  1. Log in to the HubSpot account you want to use.
  2. Select the permissions to grant, then click Connect app.

What the Connector Does

Toggling HubSpot on under + > Connectors in any chat lets Claude reference your HubSpot records in its answers. Set the connector’s Write tools option to Needs Approval, as HubSpot recommends, so Claude confirms each proposed edit with you before making it. Every create or update action is recorded in HubSpot’s Audit Log and attributed to both the user and the connector, and bulk edits run in batches of 10 records or fewer.

What Marketers Can Do Once Connected

HubSpot’s marketing examples include ranking last month’s campaigns by revenue, finding the subject lines that drew the most clicks, measuring how long contacts stayed in each lifecycle stage, and queuing follow-up tasks for recent email openers. Claude can also publish a blog post once the prompt supplies a title, author, featured image, meta description, and slug. Workflows are the exception: Claude drafts the content, and you build the workflow in HubSpot, where marketing automation runs.

Claude AI for Marketing Workflows Inside HubSpot

With the HubSpot connector in place, Claude supports four everyday marketing jobs: analyzing campaigns, drafting content and email, tailoring outreach, and even serving as a virtual assistant for routine marketing tasks. It follows the access rules already set in HubSpot, so results depend on what the signed-in user is allowed to view and change.

Campaign and Performance Analysis

Campaign records, attribution data, and marketing email performance are all readable, so one prompt can compare a campaign’s engagement with its attributed results. Prompts about individual page or post performance must name a campaign and a date range, and drafts return only metadata. Results can come back as charts, such as a pie chart isolating contacts who opened an email but never clicked. For AI analytics use cases beyond the connector, see AI marketing analytics.

Content and Email Drafting

HubSpot Content Hub supports content creation and publishing workflows. Through the connector, Claude can create and update landing pages, website pages, and marketing emails, and page designs built in Claude Design can be sent into HubSpot. Campaigns are writable too: Claude can create one and attach new assets, so a launch email and its landing page start out grouped together. Ask Claude to study your recent top-performing emails before it drafts the next one.

Personalization and Segmentation Support

Claude can read segments (lists) but can’t create them, so building segments stays in HubSpot. Use Claude instead to trace a contact’s conversations across chat, email, and SMS before tailoring outreach. Inbox and help desk conversations add another source of buyer language: Claude can summarize the month’s most common questions, surfacing recurring concerns in customers’ own words. For events, Claude can take an imported registrant list and produce follow-up emails. From there, Claude can match registrants to existing contacts and update lifecycle stages, subject to any conditional property rules configured in HubSpot.

Follow-Up, Task, and Reporting Assistance

After a sales call or campaign debrief, a single plain-language request can log the notes, create follow-up tasks, and update a contact’s lead status. Our guide on using Claude as a virtual assistant shows a comparable follow-up routine that stays inside Claude: Project instructions define how to track action items, and uploaded meeting transcripts supply the notes.

Recurring report prep suits Claude marketing automation in Claude Cowork: A skill stores your prep steps, and a scheduled task runs them remotely, even while your computer sleeps. Tasks that need local files or apps run only on your machine. Claude can then turn that prep into a team doc or a one-slide leadership summary.

Claude Prompts for Marketers Using HubSpot Context

Each prompt below opens by assigning Claude a role. Anthropic’s prompting guide lists role-setting among its core techniques and says even a one-line role steers what Claude focuses on and how it sounds. The rest names the records to pull, the work to produce, any HubSpot action, and the answer format. Swap in your own bracketed details, then save the versions that work as a team library of Claude prompts for marketers.

Pro tip: Once a prompt proves useful week after week, turn it into one of your team’s Claude skills. A skill stores the parts of a prompt that never change, like the role, the HubSpot records to check, and the output format. Claude recognizes when a request calls for that skill and applies it without being asked, so teammates only need to supply details like the campaign name and date range.

Reporting and Analytics

“You’re a marketing analyst reporting to a CMO. Pull the HubSpot campaign record and marketing email results for [Campaign Name] from [date range]. Compare open rates with click rates, break down engaged contacts by lifecycle stage, and show the campaign’s attributed revenue. Return a three-bullet summary, then a comparison table. Cite the HubSpot records behind each figure.”

Campaign Planning

This prompt grounds a Claude AI marketing strategy in deals you’ve already won:

“You’re a campaign strategist for a [industry] company. Review our closed-won deals from last quarter and identify the buying triggers that appear most often. Use them to draft a four-week launch plan for [Product] with audience criteria from our existing segments, a three-email nurture outline, and a landing page structure. Then create a campaign in HubSpot called [Campaign Name].”

The connector can’t edit a campaign once it exists, so confirm the name and details before you approve Claude’s proposal.

Content Ideation

“You’re a content marketer. Read last month’s inbox and help desk conversations in HubSpot. List the five most common questions or objections, each with a short example of how customers phrased it. Then suggest 10 blog headlines and five email subject lines that answer them in the same vocabulary.”

Email Drafting

“You’re an email copywriter focused on re-engagement. Find contacts who opened [Email Name] but didn’t click, and group them by lifecycle stage. For the largest group, draft one follow-up email that offers a 15-minute demo. For any customer example, use only these details: [case study summary]. Create it in HubSpot as a marketing email so I can review it before it goes out.”

Account and Touchpoint Summaries

“You’re a GTM strategist preparing a sales handoff. Pull the full engagement history for [Company Name] in HubSpot, including emails, meetings, calls, and notes. Summarize it in three short paragraphs: background and key stakeholders, open challenges and recent interactions, and recommended next marketing touchpoints.”

Review before you act on the output.

HubSpot acknowledges that Claude’s answers can be wrong and advises having a person check them. Adding “cite the HubSpot records behind each figure” to any analysis prompt lets you open each record and confirm the number. Before running a write prompt across many records, test it on one, and read each proposed change before typing Yes. Drafted emails and pages still need a brand voice and a link check in HubSpot before they are published.

Turning those individual checks into a repeatable team process is the job of governance.

How to Govern Claude AI for Marketing and Measure Impact

Governing Claude AI for marketing comes down to four controls: skill review, shared standards, connector access, and measurement. Together, these controls also build the readiness that HubSpot’s guide to AI agents for marketing links to success with agentic AI: clear processes and steady testing.

Set review rules for shared skills.

  • Test first: Anthropic recommends running a skill on your own account before rolling it out organization-wide.
  • Require sign-off: Set Publishing to Requires review, so nothing a teammate builds, including later edits, reaches the organization library until an owner approves it. Reviewers can’t approve their own work.
  • Scan uploads: Enterprise plans can also check each submitted version for malicious content.

Standardize terminology and claims.

  • Build a style skill: Store voice guidelines, approved product names, and banned phrases in one skill. Team and Enterprise owners can push it to everyone, and Enterprise plans can limit marketing skills to one group via a plugin.
  • Update in one place: Once an owner approves a new version of a published skill, everyone using it receives the change automatically, so a product rename gets fixed once.
  • Write verification into it: Require a source record link for every figure and a direct customer quote before any feedback summary.

Control connector access.

  • Scope access: Super Admins who approve the HubSpot connector for Claude also set its data permissions and install list.
